clue.text: The case for taking care isn't well-presented

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are set out afresh, presented in a new order

explanation.surface: Something careless is said not to be a good argument for being careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-presented' asks for CAREISNT (from 'care isn't') to be rearranged; the apostrophe is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a container, a case for holding tea, film or gas.

clue.text: Bottle displayed by artist entering a bistro

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant like a bistro
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A bottle is shown by a painter walking into a small restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass bottle or flask for serving wine or water.

clue.text: Trapped a sober individual in penury

indicators.note: in places the abstainer inside the poverty word

parts.note: need is poverty, penury
TT stands for teetotal, a person who abstains from drink

explanation.surface: A teetotaller living in poverty has been caught.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, teetotal, is a crossword convention for someone who does not drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Netted means caught as if in a mesh.

clue.text: In a beastly home gold may be hoarded

indicators.note: In places the metal inside the animal home

parts.note: a stable is a home for animals, beasts
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Treasure might be stashed away in an animal shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' means of beasts, not nasty; OR is heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something storable can be kept or stockpiled for later.

clue.text: Welshman taking a key to a vehicle

parts.note: E is a musical key
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A man from Wales takes a key to his car.
explanation.definitionFit: Evan is a typical Welsh first name, a Welsh form of John.

clue.text: May be seen about in tartan, quite composed

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: a plaid is a tartan cloth or pattern
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Something may turn up in a tartan pattern, and it all looks very calm.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa, about) goes inside PLAID; 'May be seen' only links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid describes a calm, untroubled temperament, entirely serene.

clue.text: Ran round quietly and cut off

indicators.note: round says the running word goes round the soft letter

parts.note: loped means ran with long easy strides
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone ran round softly and got cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopped means trimmed by chopping, as branches from a tree.

clue.text: Town wear

explanation.surface: Clothes for the town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardigan is a town in west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardigan is a Welsh market town, and a cardigan is a knitted jacket buttoned down the front.

clue.text: Divides the underworld classes

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
sects are classes or factions

explanation.surface: Society splits into criminal groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect is to cut apart and analyse piece by piece.

clue.text: Restrict to a pound, as appears reasonable

parts.note: to ration is to restrict supply
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Limiting someone to a pound seems a sensible economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means sensible, based on logic and sound judgment.

clue.text: Points heavenward

parts.note: read as a verb phrase it sounds like gesturing to the sky, but it describes the tall pointed tops of church towers

explanation.surface: Someone gestures towards the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Church steeples taper to a point aimed at the sky, so the tapering tops are towers pointing heavenward.

clue.text: See real possibilities of freedom

indicators.note: possibilities suggests other arrangements, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to see real chances of liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Release is liberation, being let go from captivity.

clue.text: Name of retiring adversary

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rival who is shy has his name asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns the whole run NAMEOF backwards; it looks like a description of a shy opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Foeman is an old literary word for an enemy in war.

clue.text: Exceptionally fine tree for an island resort

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A remarkably fine tree is the attraction of a holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is the largest Canary Island, a popular Spanish holiday destination.

clue.text: He'd drive an ox with little hesitation

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated ox
er is a brief sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A drover would drive an ox without pausing much.
explanation.definitionFit: A steerer is one who guides or drives, as a helmsman does a vehicle.

clue.text: Even given the apartment number

parts.note: a flat is an apartment in British usage
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone is told which apartment number they have.
explanation.definitionFit: To even something is to make it level, to smooth it down.

clue.text: Cannot tilt?

explanation.surface: A question of whether something is unable to lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannot contracts with an apostrophe to a four-letter form, and a cant is also a slope or inclination.

clue.text: Getting one's outfit into better shape is imperative!

definitions.text: Getting one's outfit into better shape

explanation.surface: An urgent need to make one's clothes look smarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing clothes smooths them into shape, and an urgent matter is one demanding attention.

clue.text: Risk setting a limit to antagonism

parts.note: an end is a limit or boundary
anger is hostility, antagonism

explanation.surface: It is risky to try to curb hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to put at risk or imperil.

clue.text: Men going on board with the wind up?

explanation.surface: People boarding a ship are frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the wind up' is British for scared; the game's pieces are called men, and draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmen are counters moved across a board, and currents of air blowing through a room are breezes.

clue.text: Call for a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A summons to buy some jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring is to telephone someone, and a ring is a band worn on the finger.

clue.text: Emus are odd as a rule

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put into an irregular order

explanation.surface: Emus are, as a general rule, peculiar birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule is a ruler, a device for measuring length.

clue.text: Control of river pests

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
lice are parasitic pests

explanation.surface: Measures to keep river vermin in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To police is to regulate or keep order.

clue.text: Hidden talent should be brought out

indicators.note: bringing out suggests developing something, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Concealed ability ought to be developed.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but not yet visible or developed.

clue.text: Not all Midsummer's Eve revels are serious

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some midsummer celebrations are rather solemn affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters come from 'Midsummer's Eve revels'; 'are serious' is the definition, a verb phrase read as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means grave or stern, not light-hearted.

clue.text: A boy in the family will become hardened

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: seed is an old word for descendants or offspring, a family line
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A youngster brought up in the household will grow tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family' is used in the biblical sense of offspring or descendants; 'will become' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned means toughened by experience, like a veteran.

clue.text: Change at going into quiet environs

indicators.note: going into says the little word enters the other word

parts.note: mute means silent or quiet

explanation.surface: Moving to a peaceful neighbourhood brings a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environs' adds nothing but surface colour, picturing the quiet surroundings that something enters.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to alter in form or nature.

clue.text: Total defeat outside an African city

indicators.note: outside says the defeat letters wrap round the other word

parts.note: KO is a knockout, a total defeat in boxing

explanation.surface: A complete loss beyond the walls of an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Kano is a major city in northern Nigeria.

clue.text: A woman needs a different make-up for riding

indicators.note: make-up is composition, so a different make-up rearranges the letters

explanation.surface: A woman requires new cosmetics before going horse riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs a different make-up for' rearranges RIDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a girl's given name, as with the actress Bergman.

clue.text: Only after money to get expensive stuff

indicators.note: after places this word behind the money word

parts.note: cash is money
mere means only or nothing more than

explanation.surface: Someone interested purely in money wants costly things.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine, costly wool fabric from Kashmir goats.

clue.text: Order a band of elastic for personal use

definitions.text: a band of elastic for personal use

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy elastic for one's own needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of the Garter is England's highest order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garter is the senior British order of knighthood, and a garter is an elastic band holding up a stocking.

clue.text: Note about one place supplying meat

indicators.note: about says the first word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
to set is to place

explanation.surface: A memo about one location supplying meat.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTE goes about I and SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a small round boneless cut of lamb.
